content.text:
Merged as `1b57c76`, conversation captured. Now your question, answered from the code rather than memory.

## No approval grant is needed — the credential already exists

The apply-stage session pushes to `.github/workflows/` using the **Claude GitHub App**, whose permissions I read off the API earlier in this session:

```
"permissions": { …, "workflows": "write", … }
```

That's the whole reason the withhold lane works: the Action's `GITHUB_TOKEN` is refused there, the app isn't. Nothing to grant, no approval prompt on that path. Eight members already proved it end to end today.

## But the world *is* stuck — and not for a reason approval fixes

You're right that something is stuck; it's the park, not a permission. Janitor rule E clears a park only for these kinds:

```js
export const SUPERSEDABLE_PARKS = Object.freeze(['failure', 'action']);
// `approval` and `decision` are absent on purpose: those parks carry content
// a person still owes an answer to … a later success does not answer them.
```

The five parked members are at **`needs-human-decision`** — a `decision` park, deliberately excluded. So a later clean converge will *not* pick them up. Tonight's run won't heal them; they'll sit until re-queued. That exclusion is correct in general — it's what stops a routine success silently closing a question someone owes an answer to — it just means these five need an explicit nudge.

So the answer to "do you need approval so the world won't be stuck" is: **no approval, but yes an action** — a re-queue of five items, which is the fleet step I flagged and haven't taken. Their staged files are still on their branches, so a re-run delivers rather than recomputing.

Two things worth flagging before I'd do it: #1540 has to reach those members first (their sessions read `task.md` from their own mount, so re-queueing before they converge just reproduces the split), and that's a fleet action rather than approved-by-LGTM work.

options.label: Baseline first, then re-queue (Recommended)
options.description: Force a fleet baseline so all 13 take claudinite-lifecycle 60831.3 and its corrected brief, confirm 13/13, then clear the task:status:* label on the five parked items so the executor re-adopts them. Their staged files survive on their branches, so the re-run delivers rather than recomputing. Ordering matters: re-queueing before the brief lands just reproduces the same split.

options.label: Wait for tonight's converge, re-queue tomorrow
options.description: Members take 60831.3 on their own nightly (dailyHour 4), then I re-queue the five. No fleet-wide action from me today. Slower, and the five stay visibly parked overnight, but every step is the ordinary mechanism rather than a forced one.

options.description: Fastest, and wrong: those members still carry the old task.md, so their sessions would read the contradictory §2 again and could park again. I would not do this.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

- session-start-hook: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code on the web. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for Claude Code on the web, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during web sessions.
- adopt-claudinite: Bootstrap Claudinite into a consuming repo — mount, hooks, checks, skills. Use when asked to bootstrap, adopt, or set up Claudinite, or to baseline a repo to pick up updates.
- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.
- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.
- ci-performance-evaluation: Method for finding where a repo's CI time actually goes and what is worth fixing. Use when CI feels slow, when investigating a runtime regression, or when the weekly ci-performance task hands you a finding.
- do-later: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked for the queue and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.
- extract-from-activity: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
- file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.
- generate-project-instructions: Decompose a project into its pack facets (working-style class, technology, aspect, domain) and extract its working instructions into reusable canon packs plus the project's own local packs (.claudinite/local_packs/). Use when a project has no established working style yet, or it exhibits a facet no pack covers — during bootstrap of a fresh/empty repo, or on an uplevel request.
- growth-dedup: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
- improve-comments: Improve the comments in a repo's own source — delete the ones that restate the code or narrate a past edit, correct the ones that have drifted from what the code now does, and add the why where only a reader's guess carries it. Use when working a repo's comments as their own pass (the tidy-repo pack's improve-comments task), never as a side effect of another change.
- production-retrospective: Design and file the review that comes back on its own once a larger element has lived in production long enough to judge — is it working, misused, overused, underused — read from its real production record against expectations written down when the element was designed. Use when designing a larger element (the brief is authored then), when filing a migration plan's chain (the retrospective is its last link), when a merge completes a design-doc'd element, or when defining a new retrospective class for a pack, a repo, or the fleet.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.
- repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
- single-issue-triage: Triage one open issue and take the first applicable action — close-if-implemented, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, or leave. Use when acting on a single issue; "implemented in main" must be verified against main's current content and the default is to comment, not close (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-issues task hands you issues to triage).
- single-pr-status: Assess one open pull request's landed status — keep-open, or closeable (merged, already-in-main, superseded, stale) — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single PR should stay open, judging by its commits and diff not its title (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-prs task hands you PRs to assess).
- unattended-agents: Architecture and practices for unattended, automation-invoked agents and recurring routines. Use when building, structuring, or running an AI agent, a scheduled routine, or a multi-stage agent pipeline.
- verify-in-production: Decide whether a change that has merged can only be proven in production, and if so file the verification that comes back on its own once it is live. Use immediately after the merge, beside the conversation capture — never before, and not on request.
- writing-claudinite-skills: Authoring or changing a skill in the Claudinite corpus — SKILL.md conventions, where a skill's checks and tests live, catalog and pack wiring. Use when creating or editing a pack's skills/<name>/ in the canon; a consumer project's own agent docs are authoring-agent-docs' turf.
- writing-handover-issues: How to write a task list a PERSON will execute — a handover issue, an adoption checklist, a "steps only a human can do" list. Use when filing or editing any issue whose body asks a human to click, set, register or copy something. Not for issues describing work you will do yourself.
- writing-migration-plans: Where a plan and a design live, and how to order a plan's phases so nothing stalls mid-run — the plan is a tracking issue (never a plan document in the repo), the design doc carries only the end state with rationale and alternatives; front-load the out-of-band setup, write ALL the code including the cleanup and take one approval for the stack, then chain every execution step to the verification of the one before it as a queued continuation, and keep the tracking issue append-only while implementing. Use BEFORE writing any DESIGN.md, migration plan, phased implementation plan, rollout or cutover plan — including the moment you are about to create a docs/<initiative>/ file — and when working through a plan's tracking issue.
- writing-tasks: The contract a Claudinite task is written to — the declaration's fields, the code-work and agentic phases, the precondition as the only decision point, ordering, and how a work item converges. Use when writing or changing a tasks/<name>/task.mjs or its worker, or when a task-declaration check fires.
- writing-tests: Practices for writing tests you can trust. Use before writing or changing any test — see-it-fail discipline, snapshot/golden rules, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, fuzzy-metric gating.
- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.

`landDelivery` was written to close for the deterministic half (#649,

credential, so you are the one who acts on it.

verified is not a smaller problem than a red check, it is the same problem with less
evidence.

**A pending PR in every case — the update did not fail.** 
ClaudiniteCanary   PR #310   open, 12:09   claudinite/update-2026-08-31-djr1ub
hitbut             PR #174   open, 12:09   claudinite/update-2026-08-31-g27eci

VascularColoring   PR #315   open, 12:09   claudinite/update-2026-08-31-gq51ij
All five still open, untouched since creation, nine hours ago. ## Why they didn't complete The update has two halves, and only the second one stopped. **The deterministic half succeeded everywhere.** It converged the mount, ran the migration, rewrote the executor, withheld that file from the pushed tree (the Actions token can't write under `.github/workflows/` — GitHub rejects the whole ref), staged it under `.claudinite/pending-workflows/`, passed `selftest --strict`, and opened the PR. Each PR body says so: > **apply-stage** — 1 withheld workflow file(s) staged under `.claudinite/pending-workflows/` > The deterministic half is done. **The agentic half refused, deliberately.** Because the terminal was `apply-stage` rather than `merge`, auto-merge is never armed — the session is meant to deliver the staged file and hand the PR to `deliver-pr.md`. Instead it read §2 of its brief, which still said a staged workflow is *"a canon bug — park it"*, and did exactly that. ClaudiniteCanary #309: > Not moving it into `.github/workflows/`, not treating it as deliverable content. Leaving PR #310 open pending a human call. So, precisely: **not a failure — a refusal that parks.** The distinction matters, because a `failure` park is in `SUPERSEDABLE_PARKS` and would clear itself on the next clean run. These are `decision` parks, which are excluded on purpose, so nothing ever revisits them. Three separate mechanisms all point the same way, and each was working as designed: 
apply-stage terminal   →  auto-merge never armed; the session must deliver
§2 of the brief        →  told the session not to; it parked instead
decision park          →  outside janitor rule E; no later run clears it
The PRs are complete and correct on their branches — the rewritten executor is staged in each. Nothing needs recomputing. What's missing is the one move the session declined: staged file → `.github/workflows/`, then deliver. That's still gated on the corrected brief reaching their mounts, which is the baseline you approved and I haven't run yet. > ⚠️ Still open: > • Five PRs pending, none failed: [ClaudiniteCanary#310](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary/pull/310), [hitbut#174](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/pull/174), [TLDR#423](https://github.com/missingbulb/TLDR/pull/423), [LaughCounter#358](https://github.com/missingbulb/LaughCounter/pull/358), [VascularColoring#315](https://github.com/missingbulb/VascularColoring/pull/315). > • Baseline + re-queue approved, **not started** — I've only been answering your questions since. > • The staged files survive on those branches, so the fix is a re-queue, not a recompute. > • No `verify-in-production` for [#1540](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1540) yet; bag test and [#1496](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1496)/[#1517](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1517) unchanged.

Is there a pending PR or did the update fail?" ## 2. Key Technical Concepts - **Claudinite**: a canon repo (`missingbulb/Claudinite`) distributing versioned "packs" to 13 fleet member repos via a vendored mount at `.claudinite/shared/`. - **Two delivery lanes**: the *engine* lane (replaces `engine/` wholesale on **every** converge; `ENGINE_VERSION` gates only migration ranges and the stamp, **not** delivery) and the *pack* lane (delivered when the canon's pack version exceeds the member's installed one). - **GitHub malicious-workflow detection** (changelog 2026-07-28): holds runs for approval; `action_required` with **zero jobs** in ~1 second, indistinguishable from "nothing was pickable". - **`toJSON(secrets)` vs `toJSON(vars)`**: the former is the flagged exfiltration shape (#1336); `vars` is GitHub-documented as non-sensitive and rendered unmasked in logs. - **The withhold lane**: `.github/workflows/` cannot be pushed with the Action's `GITHUB_TOKEN` (GitHub rejects the **whole ref**). The lane stages such writes to `.claudinite/pending-workflows/`, reports them in `withheld`, and raises an **apply stage** — an agent session running on the Claude GitHub App credential, which carries `workflows: write`. - **Park kinds**: `PARK_KINDS = ['failure','action','decision','approval']`; `SUPERSEDABLE_PARKS = ['failure','action']` — janitor rule E never clears `decision` or `approval` parks. - **Work-item lifecycle**: `create-work-item /` resolves only **existing** tasks; `--context` reaches only the agentic phase; code-work runs as a subprocess of the executor's Actions job; the agentic phase runs off-runner via a CCR routine endpoint and therefore **cannot** see executor env vars. - Version format: date-anchored `.`, e.g. `60831.3`. - Engine releases: `ENGINE_VERSION` "advanced by release, never by an ordinary change" — requires a passing live canary rehearsal plus a `engine/RELEASES.md` row citing the run. ## 3. Files and Code Sections **`packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/vars-bag.mjs`** (created, PR #1494) Reads the bag. Two deliberate departures from `secrets-bag.mjs`, documented at the site: ```js export const VARS_BAG_ENV = 'CLAUDINITE_VARS'; export const varsBag = (env = process.env) => parseBag(env[VARS_BAG_ENV]); export function varsEnv(env = process.env) { const bag = varsBag(env); if (!bag) return {}; const out = {}; for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(bag)) { if (name === VARS_BAG_ENV) continue; if (env[name] !== undefined) continue; // ADDITIVE, NEVER OVERWRITING out[name] = value; } return out; } ``` Additive-never-overwriting matters because a repo variable named `PATH` or `HOME` must not reach into a task subprocess. **`packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/env-bag.mjs`** (created) — shared `parseBag(raw)` so the two bags don't duplicate the parse. **`packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/code-work-run.mjs`** — `taskEnv` now strips both raw blobs and applies `varsEnv`: ```js export function taskEnv(names = [], env = process.env) { const out = { ...env }; delete out[SECRETS_BAG_ENV]; delete out[VARS_BAG_ENV]; for (const name of Object.keys(secretsBag(env) ?? {})) delete out[name]; return { ...out, ...varsEnv(env), ...secretsFor(names, env) }; } ``` Also holds the `::group::code_work` console.log at ~line 87 — the proposed site for the permanent bag-observability log line. **`engine/migrations/registry.mjs`** — `applyRewrites` gained the workflow guard `applyMaterializations` already had (PR #1511): ```js if (file.startsWith(WORKFLOW_DEST) && !callerCanDeliverWorkflows(env)) { done.push(`SKIPPED ${file} (workflow file; this caller cannot deliver one)`); continue; } ``` The bug: `write` dropped workflow paths silently while `done.push(file)` ran regardless — a run delivering nothing reported it had. Live in `chrome-release-vendoring`. **`packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/pack-update.mjs`** — four seams refilled (PR #1511): `write` stages workflow paths to `PENDING_DIR` and records `withheld`; `io.env` announces `{ [WITHHOLD_CAPABLE_ENV]: '1' }`; the staging sweep scoped to files this run did *not* stage; the hardcoded `const withheld = []` removed. **`packs/claudinite-tasks/migrations/2026-08-31-executor-vars-bag/migration.mjs`** (PR #1522) — a **rewrite**, not a materialize, anchored on the operator hold: ```js const EXECUTOR = '.github/workflows/claudinite-executor.yml'; const HOLD = ' CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL: ${{ vars.CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL }}\n'; appliesTo: async (read) => { const text = await read(EXECUTOR); if (!text) return false; return text.includes(HOLD) && !text.includes('CLAUDINITE_VARS:'); }, rewrite: [{ file: EXECUTOR, replace: [{ from: HOLD, to: HOLD + BAG }] }], ``` Three decisions: rewrite (a materialize would clobber each member's stamped `required_secrets`); anchored *above* the `# claudinite:secrets` marker (inside it, the wiring converge would overwrite); idempotency in `appliesTo` (split/join would otherwise double the block). **`packs/claudinite-lifecycle/tasks/update/task.md`** §2 (PR #1540) — the fix for the fleet split. ## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

# Update — the apply stage

The deterministic half already ran. Preprocessing converged this repo's mount to the
canon's current engine and pack versions, ran the version-ranged migrations, gated the
result on the converged tree's own `selftest --strict`, and opened the update PR. The
work item names the branch and says which packs moved.

**You are here for one of two reasons**, and the issue says which:

- **Withheld workflow files** — content the deterministic half already decided but its
  Action token is refused for. Nothing here needs judgment; you are the credential.
- **A pack's updated rules have met content this repo authored** and the canon has never
  seen. This is the half that needs judgment, and it is all of the judgment there is.

## 1. Read why you are here

The item's **Why the agent is here** section names the terminal and the packs
whose versions moved. That is binding scope — do not widen it.

## 2. Deliver the withheld workflow files

Only if the item's reason names them. A file under `.claudinite/pending-workflows/` is
content the deterministic half already computed and decided; it sits there because the
Action token that pushed the branch may not write under `.github/workflows/` and GitHub
rejects the WHOLE ref for trying, so putting it in the pushed tree would have failed the
entire update. You hold a credential that may write there. That is the only reason this
step is yours.

For each staged file: move `.claudinite/pending-workflows/<name>` to
`.github/workflows/<name>`, and leave the staging directory empty.

**Do not edit the content, and do not judge it.** It is what the canon computed for this
member, secrets and all; a session rewriting it is a second author of a file that has
exactly one. If the move is not obviously right — the branch carries a staged file the
item's reason does not name, or the destination already differs in a way you cannot
explain — that is the case for §5, not for improvising.

## 3. Apply the new rules

Only if the issue's reason names a migration record — it names them by path, e.g.
`packs/basics/migrations/2026-08-13-something`. **Read that record** at
`.claudinite/shared/<path>/migration.mjs`: its `applyStage.instructions` say what its
author wanted done, in their words, and are the specific half of this section. The
record is on the branch you were given because the update that raised it vendored it
there. A record the issue names but the branch does not carry is a park
(§5) — guessing at what its author wanted is worse than reporting it missing.

Then, on that branch:

- Bring this repo's own content in line with the updated pack rules, and repair the
  tests those rules break.
- Nothing outside that scope. No new features, no unrelated tidy-ups, no rewriting a
  member-authored local pack beyond what the new rules require.

## 4. Verify the executor routine

The one check no Action can make. This repo's executor routine is fired by an API
call to the endpoint its config names, and it is not a GitHub artifact — only a
session can see it. Confirm it exists and that its whole stored prompt is the one
line pointing at the mounted queue instructions
(`.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/instructions.md`): everything a task
session does comes from that file, so a prompt carrying instructions of its own is
behavior nobody reviews. Report what you found either way.

## 5. End green, or park

Run this repo's checks. Green: push to the branch, then hand the PR to the shared
delivery procedure — `deliver-pr.md`, at the root of the claudinite-tasks pack
(`.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/deliver-pr.md`; the canon runs it from
`packs/claudinite-tasks/`) — and do what it says. Nothing else will land this PR:
the deterministic half arms auto-merge only on a `merge` terminal, and yours was
`apply-stage`, so it sits unarmed until you deliver it.

Not green, or a repair you are not sure of: leave the PR open, label
it `task:status:needs-human-decision`, and say in one comment what is unresolved. A withheld workflow you did
not deliver is "not green" — it stays owed, and the next cycle will stage it again.

**Why the delivery is yours to run rather than left for later.** An unmerged PR is not lost — the next
cycle's disposal merges a green one. But `update` is a **daily** task, so "the next
cycle" is up to a day away, and until then a workflow you moved into
`.github/workflows/` on the branch is not in `.github/workflows/` on `main`. That
standing ~24h offset between a run's output and the member's `main` is the exact defect
`landDelivery` was written to close for the deterministic half (#649,
`packs/claudinite-tasks/land-pr.mjs`): *the evidence that settles it does not take a day to
arrive*. The same reasoning binds here — the only difference is that you hold the
credential, so you are the one who acts on it.

Every non-green end looks the same here, and that is the point — a repair nobody
verified is not a smaller problem than a red check, it is the same problem with less
evidence.

+// Put the repository-variable bag into every member's live executor workflow (#1509).
+//
+// WHAT IT DELIVERS. #1494 added `CLAUDINITE_VARS: ${{ toJSON(vars) }}` to the executor
+// STUB and shipped the reader (queue/vars-bag.mjs). A stub is scaffolded once at
+// adoption, so every member already running the queue holds the reader and no line for
+// it to read — `varsEnv` finds no bag and contributes nothing, which is safe but inert.
+// This record is what closes that gap on a member that adopted before #1494.
+//
+// A REWRITE, NOT A MATERIALIZE. The executor is not identical across members: the wiring
+// converge stamps each one's own `required_secrets` beneath the `# claudinite:secrets`
+// marker. Copying the stub over it would deliver the line and take every member's
+// secrets with it, which is a far worse outcome than the gap this closes. A rewrite
+// preserves everything it does not name — the same reason static-website's record
+// rewrites rather than replaces.
+//
+// IDEMPOTENCY LIVES IN `appliesTo`, not in the replacement. `applyRewrites` uses
+// split/join, so running this twice against an already-rewritten file would insert a
+// SECOND copy of the block; the version gate makes that unlikely and `appliesTo` makes
+// it impossible. Both halves are load-bearing.
+//
+// THE ANCHOR is the operator hold, which every member's executor carries — the stub
+// guard in converge-workflows.test.mjs pins it in both stubs, and it has been in the
+// file since the hold shipped. Anchoring to the `# claudinite:secrets` marker instead
+// would put the bag inside the converge's stamped region, where the next wiring
+// converge would regenerate over it.
+const EXECUTOR = '.github/workflows/claudinite-executor.yml';
+const HOLD = '          CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL: ${{ vars.CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL }}\n';
+const BAG = `          # Every repository VARIABLE, as one static line (#1492). Unlike the secrets
+          # below this never changes: \`vars\` is the context GitHub's own docs define as
+          # non-sensitive and render unmasked in logs, so serialising it is not the
+          # exfiltration shape that gets a workflow held for approval (#1336) — and this
+          # file is the one path a converge cannot write, so keeping it independent of
+          # what any task declares is worth a great deal. vars-bag.mjs is the reader.
+          CLAUDINITE_VARS: \${{ toJSON(vars) }}
+`;
+
+export default {
+  id: 'executor-vars-bag',
+  landed: '2026-08-31',
+  version: '60831.6',
+  summary: 'the live executor workflow carries CLAUDINITE_VARS, so a task can read a repo variable the workflow never names (#1492, #1494)',
+
+  // Two conditions, both required: the member runs the queue (it has an executor with
+  // the hold to anchor to), and it does not already carry the bag. The second is what
+  // makes a re-run a no-op rather than a doubled block.
+  appliesTo: async (read) => {
+    const text = await read(EXECUTOR);
+    if (!text) return false;
+    return text.includes(HOLD) && !text.includes('CLAUDINITE_VARS:');
+  },
+
+  rewrite: [{ file: EXECUTOR, replace: [{ from: HOLD, to: HOLD + BAG }] }],
+
+  // The old shape is an executor with no bag — exactly what `appliesTo` tests, so a
+  // member is "still legacy" on the same condition that makes this record apply.
+  legacyPresent: async (_exists, read) => {
+    const text = await read(EXECUTOR);
+    return Boolean(text) && text.includes(HOLD) && !text.includes('CLAUDINITE_VARS:');
+  },
+};"},{"filename":".claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/pack.mjs","status":"modified","additions":1,"deletions":1,"changes":2,"patch":"@@ -31,7 +31,7 @@

+//
+// WHAT IT DELIVERS. #1494 added `CLAUDINITE_VARS: ${{ toJSON(vars) }}` to the executor
+// STUB and shipped the reader (queue/vars-bag.mjs). A stub is scaffolded once at
+// adoption, so every member already running the queue holds the reader and no line for
+// it to read — `varsEnv` finds no bag and contributes nothing, which is safe but inert.
+// This record is what closes that gap on a member that adopted before #1494.
+//
+// A REWRITE, NOT A MATERIALIZE. The executor is not identical across members: the wiring
+// converge stamps each one's own `required_secrets` beneath the `# claudinite:secrets`
+// marker. Copying the stub over it would deliver the line and take every member's
+// secrets with it, which is a far worse outcome than the gap this closes. A rewrite
+// preserves everything it does not name — the same reason static-website's record
+// rewrites rather than replaces.

+// split/join, so running this twice against an already-rewritten file would insert a
+// SECOND copy of the block; the version gate makes that unlikely and `appliesTo` makes
+// it impossible. Both halves are load-bearing.
+//
+// THE ANCHOR is the operator hold, which every member's executor carries — the stub
+// guard in converge-workflows.test.mjs pins it in both stubs, and it has been in the
+// file since the hold shipped. Anchoring to the `# claudinite:secrets` marker instead
+// would put the bag inside the converge's stamped region, where the next wiring
+// converge would regenerate over it.
+const EXECUTOR = '.github/workflows/claudinite-executor.yml';
+const HOLD = '          CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL: ${{ vars.CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL }}\n';
+const BAG = `          # Every repository VARIABLE, as one static line (#1492). Unlike the secrets
+          # below this never changes: \`vars\` is the context GitHub's own docs define as
+          # non-sensitive and render unmasked in logs, so serialising it is not the
+          # exfiltration shape that gets a workflow held for approval (#1336) — and this
+          # file is the one path a converge cannot write, so keeping it independent of
+          # what any task declares is worth a great deal. vars-bag.mjs is the reader.
+          CLAUDINITE_VARS: \${{ toJSON(vars) }}
+`;
+
+export default {
+  id: 'executor-vars-bag',
+  landed: '2026-08-31',
+  version: '60831.6',
+  summary: 'the live executor workflow carries CLAUDINITE_VARS, so a task can read a repo variable the workflow never names (#1492, #1494)',

+  // the hold to anchor to), and it does not already carry the bag. The second is what
+  // makes a re-run a no-op rather than a doubled block.
+  appliesTo: async (read) => {
+    const text = await read(EXECUTOR);
+    if (!text) return false;
+    return text.includes(HOLD) && !text.includes('CLAUDINITE_VARS:');

+  // member is "still legacy" on the same condition that makes this record apply.
+  legacyPresent: async (_exists, read) => {
+    const text = await read(EXECUTOR);

I re-read all three from source. **Only one of the three was a bug, it's already fixed, and changing either of the other two would actively hurt.** One of those harms is live right now, because you've approved the PRs. ## The three, judged ### 1. `apply-stage` never arms auto-merge — must not change `worker.mjs:225` arms delivery on exactly one terminal: ```js if (terminal.action === 'merge') await landDelivery({ token, repo, base, pr, delivery }); ``` I checked what merging PR #310 would actually deliver. The file list is decisive — it **adds** `.claudinite/pending-workflows/claudinite-executor.yml` and **does not touch** `.github/workflows/claudinite-executor.yml`. The bag line exists only at the staging path. So auto-merging an apply-stage PR would land a copy of the executor into a directory Actions never reads, leave the real workflow unchanged, and report the update delivered. The withheld case is the one where merging early is *most* wrong, because the branch does not yet contain the thing the run exists to deliver. `terminals.mjs` says it in the precedence comment — "merging first would call that reconciliation optional" — and the file list is that comment being right. ### 2. §2 of the brief — this was the whole bug, already fixed The retired sentence told the session a staged workflow was a canon bug to park. That's gone in `claudinite-lifecycle` **60831.3**, replaced by "## 2. Deliver the withheld workflow files," and `engine-tests/install.test.mjs` now refuses the old sentence's return. Nothing further to change — it just hasn't reached the five members' mounts, which is what the baseline does. ### 3. The decision park — I was wrong, nothing needs changing I told you nothing self-heals these. That was wrong, and the item says so itself. ClaudiniteCanary **#309**'s body carries: ``` Ends-when: #310 closed ``` Janitor **rule G** (`janitor-rules.mjs:220`) reads exactly that field, and its header names this case: rule E excludes approval/decision parks *precisely because* they hold an open PR, and rule G is what answers them. `resolutionOf(310)` returns null while the PR is open, so the park correctly stands. Merged → `done`; closed unmerged → `rejected`. So the recovery path exists and is working. Adding `decision` to `SUPERSEDABLE_PARKS` would be the damaging change: it would let any later clean nightly `update` run close a park whose PR is still open and undelivered — the exact confusion rule E's comment was written to prevent. ## The live consequence of the approvals Rule G reads merged-ness. If those five PRs merge as they stand, each item closes **`done`** — "nothing is left for anyone to act on" — while the workflow is still sitting in `pending-workflows/` and the live executor still has no `CLAUDINITE_VARS`. It self-heals a cycle later (`appliesTo` still fires on a live executor lacking the bag, and `stagedFiles` sweeps the previous cycle's leftovers), but you'd spend a day with five items recorded as delivered that weren't. The approval doesn't unblock them. What unblocks them is the corrected brief reaching their mounts and the item being re-queued so a session moves the file onto the *same* branch — then the PR merges complete. 
mechanism                        verdict         change it?
apply-stage ≠ merge              working         no — merging early is the defect
task.md §2                       WAS the bug     already fixed, 60831.3, undelivered
decision park not superseded     working         no — rule G covers it via Ends-when
The single fix is the one already made. The fleet split was one contradictory sentence, not three mechanisms.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.

Answering the analysis question first, then executing the approved path. ## The three mechanisms, judged I named three reasons. Reading the source, **only one of them was a defect, and it's already fixed.** Changing either of the other two would actively hurt — and one of those harms is live right now. ### 1. `apply-stage` never arms auto-merge — must not change `terminals.mjs` states the precedence deliberately: *"It is NOT a merge: the rules have landed but nothing has yet reconciled them with the member's own content, and merging first would call that reconciliation optional."* That's not abstract here. I pulled the file list of ClaudiniteCanary [#310](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary/pull/310): 
.claudinite/pending-workflows/claudinite-executor.yml   ADDED   (80 lines, carries CLAUDINITE_VARS)
.github/workflows/claudinite-executor.yml               UNTOUCHED
The workflow is staged, not delivered. **Auto-merging an apply-stage PR would land a PR whose entire purpose is undone** — the executor on `main` still has no `CLAUDINITE_VARS`, and the migration's `appliesTo` stays true forever. Arming auto-merge here doesn't make the update work; it makes the update silently not work while reporting success. This mechanism is what's protecting you. ### 2. §2 of the brief — this was the bug, already fixed The one real defect. It told the session a staged workflow was a canon bug and to park it. Fixed in `claudinite-lifecycle` **60831.3**, which is in canon `main` but not on members — they're on 60831.1. That's the whole gap. ### 3. Decision parks aren't superseded — **I was wrong; nothing needs changing** I said nothing self-heals these. That's incorrect. Item [#309](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary/issues/309) carries: ``` Ends-when: #310 closed ``` Janitor **rule G** reads exactly that field and closes the item when the target resolves — `done` if merged, `rejected` if closed unmerged. Rule E's exclusion of `decision`/`approval` is precisely *because* rule G owns them. The coverage is complete; loosening `SUPERSEDABLE_PARKS` would break the thing that already works. ### The consequence for the approvals you just gave Those two facts combine into a live hazard. If the five PRs merge as they stand: the staged file lands inert, the live executor still has no bag, and rule G closes all five items **`done`** — five runs recorded as delivered that delivered nothing. That's why I asked before touching them, and why the baseline-then-re-queue path is the one that makes your approvals apply to a PR that actually carries the workflow. Now executing it.

The mount is already converged onto the packs that support it; what is left is one sitting of settings work plus one workflow PR.

- [ ] Register a GitHub App named `Claudinite Dashboard` — [new App](https://github.com/settings/apps/new)
- [ ] Set its **Homepage URL** and **Callback URL** to `https://missingbulb.github.io/`, and tick **Enable wildcard matching** beneath the callback
- [ ] Tick *Request user authorization (OAuth) during installation*
- [ ] Under **Permissions → Repository**, set Contents, Issues, Metadata and Actions to **Read-only**, then press **Create GitHub App**
- [ ] Copy the **Client ID** — on the App's General page, under the app name; begins `Iv23`
- [ ] Press **Generate a new client secret** on that same page, and copy the value shown under **Client secrets** — displayed once
- [ ] Install the App on `missingbulb` — the **Install App** tab in that page's left sidebar
- [ ] Copy your Cloudflare **Account ID** — [Workers overview](https://dash.cloudflare.com/?to=/:account/workers), right-hand sidebar under *Account details*; 32 hex characters
- [ ] Create a Cloudflare API token from the **Edit Cloudflare Workers** template — [new token](https://dash.cloudflare.com/profile/api-tokens); copy the value shown once on the confirmation screen
- [ ] Add secret `GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` (the client secret) — [new secret](https://github.com/missingbulb/Shepherd/settings/secrets/actions/new)
- [ ] Add secret `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` (the API token) — [new secret](https://github.com/missingbulb/Shepherd/settings/secrets/actions/new)
- [ ] Add variable `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` (the Account ID) — [new variable](https://github.com/missingbulb/Shepherd/settings/variables/actions/new)
- [ ] Add variable `CLAUDINITE_DASHBOARD_CLIENT_ID` (the Client ID) — [new variable](https://github.com/missingbulb/Shepherd/settings/variables/actions/new)
- [ ] Merge the PR that re-seeds `.github/workflows/claudinite-dashboard-pages.yml` from the pack's current stub
- [ ] Run the deploy: `create-work-item claudinite-dashboard/deploy-oauth-exchange`, and copy the `https://…workers.dev` URL it reports
- [ ] Add variable `CLAUDINITE_DASHBOARD_EXCHANGE_URL` (that URL) — [new variable](https://github.com/missingbulb/Shepherd/settings/variables/actions/new)

**Done when** loading the [dashboard](https://missingbulb.github.io/Shepherd/) in a signed-out window shows **Sign in with GitHub**, and clicking it returns you signed in with the rate pill reading `…/5000 · user`.

---

## Background

**Why.** Every viewer of the dashboard today reads GitHub anonymously at 60 requests/hour per IP — which one fleet sweep exceeds — or pastes a token. A static page cannot reuse your github.com login, so a Sign in button is the only alternative, and it needs an App plus a hosted `code` → token exchange.

**What each part buys, and what stays broken until it is done:**

| Undone | Effect |
|---|---|
| The App is not registered | No Sign in button renders anywhere; the token box is the only way in |
| The App is not installed on `missingbulb` | Sign-in succeeds, but every member row reads *not visible to you* — the token carries no installation |
| Either secret is missing | The deploy run parks at `task:status:needs-human-action` naming it; nothing else breaks |
| `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` is missing | The deploy fails naming it — nothing declares it, so the queue cannot park on it |
| The workflow is not re-seeded | The sign-in variables never reach the site build, so the button never appears however they are set |
| `CLAUDINITE_DASHBOARD_EXCHANGE_URL` is unset | The page renders the token box; the client id alone does nothing |

**The workflow re-seed is overdue for a second reason.** This repo's seeded copy still watches `.claudinite-checks.json` — in both its `push` path filter and its deploy cache key — rather than `.claudinite-settings.json`, which is where this repo's dashboard config actually lives. It has been that way since the settings-file rename; `.github/workflows/` is the one path a converge cannot write, so the stub's fix never reached it. Today that means **a config change does not republish the site at all**. Re-seeding fixes that and adds the two `vars` lines in the same PR.

**Why some of these are variables and not secrets.** Neither the client id nor the exchange URL is confidential — the first is in every authorize URL the page builds, the second is fetched by the browser. The Cloudflare account id is in every dashboard URL you open. Secrets are only the two real credentials.

**Why the API token is that narrow.** The *Edit Cloudflare Workers* template grants Workers Scripts · Edit and nothing else. The deploy uploads one script and reads the account's `workers.dev` subdomain; it needs no more.

The mount is already converged onto the packs that support it; what is left is one sitting of settings work plus one workflow PR.

- [ ] Register a GitHub App named `Claudinite Dashboard` — [new App](https://github.com/settings/apps/new)
- [ ] Set its **Homepage URL** and **Callback URL** to `https://missingbulb.github.io/`, and tick **Enable wildcard matching** beneath the callback
- [ ] Tick *Request user authorization (OAuth) during installation*
- [ ] Under **Permissions → Repository**, set Contents, Issues, Metadata and Actions to **Read-only**, then press **Create GitHub App**
- [ ] Copy the **Client ID** — on the App's General page, under the app name; begins `Iv23`
- [ ] Press **Generate a new client secret** on that same page, and copy the value shown under **Client secrets** — displayed once
- [ ] Install the App on `missingbulb` — the **Install App** tab in that page's left sidebar
- [ ] Copy your Cloudflare **Account ID** — [Workers overview](https://dash.cloudflare.com/?to=/:account/workers), right-hand sidebar under *Account details*; 32 hex characters
- [ ] Create a Cloudflare API token from the **Edit Cloudflare Workers** template — [new token](https://dash.cloudflare.com/profile/api-tokens); copy the value shown once on the confirmation screen
- [ ] Add secret `GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` (the client secret) — [new secret](https://github.com/missingbulb/Shepherd/settings/secrets/actions/new)
- [ ] Add secret `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` (the API token) — [new secret](https://github.com/missingbulb/Shepherd/settings/secrets/actions/new)
- [ ] Add variable `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` (the Account ID) — [new variable](https://github.com/missingbulb/Shepherd/settings/variables/actions/new)
- [ ] Add variable `CLAUDINITE_DASHBOARD_CLIENT_ID` (the Client ID) — [new variable](https://github.com/missingbulb/Shepherd/settings/variables/actions/new)
- [ ] Merge the PR that re-seeds `.github/workflows/claudinite-dashboard-pages.yml` from the pack's current stub
- [ ] Run the deploy: `create-work-item claudinite-dashboard/deploy-oauth-exchange`, and copy the `https://…workers.dev` URL it reports
- [ ] Add variable `CLAUDINITE_DASHBOARD_EXCHANGE_URL` (that URL) — [new variable](https://github.com/missingbulb/Shepherd/settings/variables/actions/new)

**Done when** loading the [dashboard](https://missingbulb.github.io/Shepherd/) in a signed-out window shows **Sign in with GitHub**, and clicking it returns you signed in with the rate pill reading `…/5000 · user`.

---

## Background

**Why.** Every viewer of the dashboard today reads GitHub anonymously at 60 requests/hour per IP — which one fleet sweep exceeds — or pastes a token. A static page cannot reuse your github.com login, so a Sign in button is the only alternative, and it needs an App plus a hosted `code` → token exchange.

**What each part buys, and what stays broken until it is done:**

| Undone | Effect |
|---|---|
| The App is not registered | No Sign in button renders anywhere; the token box is the only way in |
| The App is not installed on `missingbulb` | Sign-in succeeds, but every member row reads *not visible to you* — the token carries no installation |
| Either secret is missing | The deploy run parks at `task:status:needs-human-action` naming it; nothing else breaks |
| `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` is missing | The deploy fails naming it — nothing declares it, so the queue cannot park on it |
| The workflow is not re-seeded | The sign-in variables never reach the site build, so the button never appears however they are set |
| `CLAUDINITE_DASHBOARD_EXCHANGE_URL` is unset | The page renders the token box; the client id alone does nothing |

**The workflow re-seed is overdue for a second reason.** This repo's seeded copy still watches `.claudinite-checks.json` — in both its `push` path filter and its deploy cache key — rather than `.claudinite-settings.json`, which is where this repo's dashboard config actually lives. It has been that way since the settings-file rename; `.github/workflows/` is the one path a converge cannot write, so the stub's fix never reached it. Today that means **a config change does not republish the site at all**. Re-seeding fixes that and adds the two `vars` lines in the same PR.

**Why some of these are variables and not secrets.** Neither the client id nor the exchange URL is confidential — the first is in every authorize URL the page builds, the second is fetched by the browser. The Cloudflare account id is in every dashboard URL you open. Secrets are only the two real credentials.

**Why the API token is that narrow.** The *Edit Cloudflare Workers* template grants Workers Scripts · Edit and nothing else. The deploy uploads one script and reads the account's `workers.dev` subdomain; it needs no more.

The baseline is running. Here's where things stand while it follows the fleet. ## What I did with the three mechanisms: changed none of them Your question was whether loosening them would hurt. The answer is that **two of the three are load-bearing and one wasn't a mechanism at all — it was my mistake.** 
1. apply-stage never auto-merges   KEEP — proven by #310's file list; loosening
                                   it lands the PR with the workflow undelivered
2. §2 said "park it"               FIXED already, in 60831.3 (#1540)
3. decision parks never superseded  NOT A GAP — rule G owns them via Ends-when
Only one instruction ever needed changing, and it already changed. That's the whole repair. ## What I found on the way **The baseline's own failure was correct behaviour.** [Shepherd#377](https://github.com/missingbulb/Shepherd/issues/377) exited 1 with: > `5 of 13 dispatched member(s) did not reach canon's versions … this run fails rather than counting the dispatch as the outcome` Exactly the five. It refused to report a dispatch as a delivery — the same principle as #1 above, one layer up. **The re-queue and the baseline turned out to be one lever, not two.** `force-fleet-baseline.mjs` dispatches each member's scheduler with `wake: update`, and those five parked items are the standing `update` items (`task:origin:planned`). The wake is the sanctioned road out of `needs-human`, so pushing 60831.3 and un-parking the five is a single action. I'd planned them as two steps; the code says otherwise. **Shepherd merged its own update meanwhile** — `Claudinite update: 4 packs upgraded (#381)` — so the enforcer is on 60831.3 before it dispatches. ## Actions taken - Created [Shepherd#382](https://github.com/missingbulb/Shepherd/issues/382), the forced baseline, carrying the context for what changed and what to expect per member. - Closed [#377](https://github.com/missingbulb/Shepherd/issues/377) `task:obsolete` / `not_planned` with the supersession comment — the exact sequence `createWorkItem` performs, made with my own tools since `api.github.com` is proxy-blocked here. - [Run 33444514284](https://github.com/missingbulb/Shepherd/actions/runs/33444514284) picked it up within seconds. I did **not** merge the five PRs you approved. As they stand they'd land the executor into `.claudinite/pending-workflows/` only, leave the live workflow without `CLAUDINITE_VARS`, and let rule G close all five items `done` — five deliveries recorded that didn't happen. After this run they should carry the file at its real path, and your approvals will apply to a PR that actually delivers. > ⚠️ In flight: > • [Shepherd#382](https://github.com/missingbulb/Shepherd/issues/382) running — dispatches 13, follows to canon's versions, ~20 min. I'm holding to watch it terminal. > • The five PRs stay unmerged by design until their apply stage moves the workflow: [ClaudiniteCanary#310](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary/pull/310), [hitbut#174](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/pull/174), [TLDR#423](https://github.com/missingbulb/TLDR/pull/423), [LaughCounter#358](https://github.com/missingbulb/LaughCounter/pull/358), [VascularColoring#315](https://github.com/missingbulb/VascularColoring/pull/315). > • No code changed this turn — the fix was already in canon; this was delivery. > • Still untouched: the bag has no consumer and has never been read in a real run; `verify-in-production` for [#1540](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1540) unfiled; the 47-PR fleet backlog.

        type: string

permissions:
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write
  actions: write

jobs:
  execute:
    # A workflow's event trigger names label strings LITERALLY — nothing here
    # decodes — so both ready spellings must appear for as long as any fielded
    # engine writes the legacy one (#1119).
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
      || github.event.label.name == 'task:status:waiting-for-executor'
      || github.event.label.name == 'task:ready'
      || github.event.label.name == 'task:urgent'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # A backstop against a wedged runner, well clear of any declared
    # `code_work_timeout`; the heartbeat's leash is what bounds real work.
    timeout-minutes: 350
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Pick up and execute ready work
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL: ${{ vars.CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL }}
          # Every repository VARIABLE, as one static line (#1492). Unlike the secrets
          # below this never changes: `vars` is the context GitHub's own docs define as
          # non-sensitive and render unmasked in logs, so serialising it is not the
          # exfiltration shape that gets a workflow held for approval (#1336) — and this
          # file is the one path a converge cannot write, so keeping it independent of
          # what any task declares is worth a great deal. vars-bag.mjs is the reader.
          CLAUDINITE_VARS: ${{ toJSON(vars) }}
          # Every declared task's `required_secrets`, plus the configured endpoint
          # tokens, regenerated by the wiring converge. Actions requires each secret
          # to be named statically, so this list is the whole delivery mechanism; a
          # worker then reads process.env.<NAME>.
          #
          # The converge writes the list directly beneath this line, so it stays last.
          # claudinite:secrets
          CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN }}
          FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/executor.mjs

  continue-the-chain:
    needs: execute
    if: failure() || cancelled()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      actions: write
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Continue the drain, or escalate a chain that keeps dying
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          CLAUDINITE_CONTINUATION_DEPTH: ${{ inputs.continuation_depth }}
        run: node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/executor-continuation.mjs

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.
