- session-start-hook: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code on the web. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for Claude Code on the web, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during web sessions.
- adopt-claudinite: Bootstrap Claudinite into a consuming repo — mount, hooks, checks, skills. Use when asked to bootstrap, adopt, or set up Claudinite, or to baseline a repo to pick up updates.
- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.
- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.
- ci-performance-evaluation: Method for finding where a repo's CI time actually goes and what is worth fixing. Use when CI feels slow, when investigating a runtime regression, or when the weekly ci-performance task hands you a finding.
- do-later: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked for the queue and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.
- extract-from-activity: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
- file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.
- generate-project-instructions: Decompose a project into its pack facets (working-style class, technology, aspect, domain) and extract its working instructions into reusable canon packs plus the project's own local packs (.claudinite/local_packs/). Use when a project has no established working style yet, or it exhibits a facet no pack covers — during bootstrap of a fresh/empty repo, or on an uplevel request.
- growth-dedup: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
- improve-comments: Improve the comments in a repo's own source — delete the ones that restate the code or narrate a past edit, correct the ones that have drifted from what the code now does, and add the why where only a reader's guess carries it. Use when working a repo's comments as their own pass (the tidy-repo pack's improve-comments task), never as a side effect of another change.
- production-retrospective: Design and file the review that comes back on its own once a larger element has lived in production long enough to judge — is it working, misused, overused, underused — read from its real production record against expectations written down when the element was designed. Use when designing a larger element (the brief is authored then), when filing a migration plan's chain (the retrospective is its last link), when a merge completes a design-doc'd element, or when defining a new retrospective class for a pack, a repo, or the fleet.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.
- repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
- single-issue-triage: Triage one open issue and take the first applicable action — close-if-implemented, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, or leave. Use when acting on a single issue; "implemented in main" must be verified against main's current content and the default is to comment, not close (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-issues task hands you issues to triage).
- single-pr-status: Assess one open pull request's landed status — keep-open, or closeable (merged, already-in-main, superseded, stale) — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single PR should stay open, judging by its commits and diff not its title (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-prs task hands you PRs to assess).
- unattended-agents: Architecture and practices for unattended, automation-invoked agents and recurring routines. Use when building, structuring, or running an AI agent, a scheduled routine, or a multi-stage agent pipeline.
- verify-in-production: Decide whether a change that has merged can only be proven in production, and if so file the verification that comes back on its own once it is live. Use immediately after the merge, beside the conversation capture — never before, and not on request.
- writing-claudinite-skills: Authoring or changing a skill in the Claudinite corpus — SKILL.md conventions, where a skill's checks and tests live, catalog and pack wiring. Use when creating or editing a pack's skills/<name>/ in the canon; a consumer project's own agent docs are authoring-agent-docs' turf.
- writing-handover-issues: How to write a task list a PERSON will execute — a handover issue, an adoption checklist, a "steps only a human can do" list. Use when filing or editing any issue whose body asks a human to click, set, register or copy something. Not for issues describing work you will do yourself.
- writing-migration-plans: Where a plan and a design live, and how to order a plan's phases so nothing stalls mid-run — the plan is a tracking issue (never a plan document in the repo), the design doc carries only the end state with rationale and alternatives; front-load the out-of-band setup, write ALL the code including the cleanup and take one approval for the stack, then chain every execution step to the verification of the one before it as a queued continuation, and keep the tracking issue append-only while implementing. - writing-tasks: The contract a Claudinite task is written to — the declaration's fields, the code-work and agentic phases, the precondition as the only decision point, ordering, and how a work item converges. Use when writing or changing a tasks/<name>/task.mjs or its worker, or when a task-declaration check fires.
- writing-tests: Practices for writing tests you can trust. Use before writing or changing any test — see-it-fail discipline, snapshot/golden rules, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, fuzzy-metric gating.
- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. input.title: A withheld workflow file is lost silently and permanently when its update PR merges before the apply stage delivers it
input.body:
Five members ended up stamped past a migration record without ever receiving what it delivers, and every signal reported success. The loss is unrecoverable by any later converge.

## What happened

`claudinite-tasks` 60831.6 carries `2026-08-31-executor-vars-bag`, a rewrite putting `CLAUDINITE_VARS: ${{ toJSON(vars) }}` into each member's live `.github/workflows/claudinite-executor.yml`. Because a converge's `GITHUB_TOKEN` may not write under `.github/workflows/`, the withhold lane stages it to `.claudinite/pending-workflows/` and raises an `apply-stage` terminal; the apply-stage session, holding a credential that may write there, is what moves it into place.

On five members that session parked instead (a separate bug, fixed in `claudinite-lifecycle` 60831.3), leaving the update PR open with the file staged. Those PRs were then merged by hand. That is where this bug starts:

1. The merge lands `.claudinite-settings.json` stamping `claudinite-tasks` 60831.6 — **the stamp advances even though the withheld file was never delivered.**
2. The next converge's staging sweep clears `.claudinite/pending-workflows/`, correctly reading the file as a previous cycle's leftover. The staged copy is gone.
3. `migrationApplies` is `want > have` (`engine/checks/helpers/active-migrations.mjs:171`). The member is now at or above 60831.6, so the record no longer applies — vendoring stops fetching it and it is removed from the mount.

Net: the live workflow lacks the line, the staged copy is deleted, and the record that would restore it can never reach that member again. Nothing is red anywhere.

## Confirmed state

All five, identically — `CLAUDINITE_VARS` absent from the live executor, `claudinite-tasks` stamped `60831.9`, the record absent from the mount, `.claudinite/pending-workflows/` empty:

- missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary (PR #310, then #311 which shows `removed` for both the staged file and the record)
- missingbulb/hitbut, missingbulb/TLDR, missingbulb/LaughCounter, missingbulb/VascularColoring

The other eight delivered normally and carry the line.

## Why it stayed invisible

- `fleet-baseline` follows members to **canon's stamped versions**, which are current. A forced baseline reported success in 4m35s while all five were missing the delivery.
- The update run itself is green: the deterministic half genuinely did everything asked of it.
- The apply-stage park is the only signal, and merging the PR resolves it — janitor rule G reads the merge and closes the item `task:status:done`, i.e. "nothing is left for anyone to act on", for a delivery that never happened.

## Candidate fixes

Both are worth having; the first is the root cause.

1. **Do not advance the stamp while a withheld file is undelivered.** The stamp is the claim that the member received the version. A run that withheld something has not delivered that version, so it should not stamp it — leaving the record applicable and the next converge able to re-stage.
2. **Do not sweep a staged file that was never delivered.** The sweep's premise is that a staged file is a leftover of a completed cycle. A file whose destination still lacks its content is not a leftover; it is the outstanding delivery.

Either alone would have made this recoverable. Both together also make the failure visible rather than silent.

A test must see the loss happen before the fix: converge with a withheld file, merge without delivering, converge again, and assert the destination still lacks the content while the record has gone out of scope.

## Not in scope here

Re-delivering the line to the five is a separate change — a re-issued record at a new version, whose `appliesTo` already no-ops on the eight that have it.

git add -A && git commit -q -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Hold a pack's stamp while it still owes a withheld workflow file

A migration record targeting .github/workflows/ is staged rather than
written: the converge's GITHUB_TOKEN may not push there, so the apply
stage delivers it on a credential that may. The run stamped the owning
pack anyway, which claims a delivery that has not happened.

That claim is unrecoverable rather than merely early. migrationApplies
is `want > have`, so the moment the stamp lands the record stops
applying and stops vendoring, and the next cycle sweeps the staged copy
as a leftover — removing the last source of the content. Nothing is red
at any point: the run is green, the stamp reads current, and a fleet
baseline that follows members to canon's versions reports success.

Five members reached exactly that state when their apply-stage PRs were
merged by hand before the stage delivered the withheld executor.

The stamp now skips a pack that finished the run owing a withheld file,
scoped to that pack rather than the whole run. The record stays in
range, so the next cycle stages the delivery again.

Refs #1545
EOF

input.title: Never stamp a pack that still owes a withheld workflow file, and re-reach the five members it stranded
input.body:
Closes #1545

Five members are stamped past `claudinite-tasks` 60831.6 with no `CLAUDINITE_VARS` line in their live executor, and no converge can reach them. This fixes the cause and re-opens a route to the five.

## The defect

A migration record targeting `.github/workflows/` cannot be written by the converge — GitHub rejects the whole ref for a `GITHUB_TOKEN` push under that path — so the withhold lane stages it to `.claudinite/pending-workflows/` and the apply stage delivers it on a credential that may write there.

The run stamped the owning pack regardless. That is a claim to have received a version whose delivery has not happened, and it is unrecoverable rather than merely early:

1. `migrationApplies` is `want > have`, so the stamp immediately puts the record out of range — it stops applying and stops vendoring.
2. The next cycle's staging sweep correctly reads the undelivered file as a previous cycle's leftover and deletes it.

Both copies of the content are then gone and nothing can recreate them. Every signal stays green throughout: the run succeeds, the stamp reads current, and `fleet-baseline` — which follows members to canon's stamped versions — reports success. A forced baseline did exactly that in 4m35s while five members were missing the delivery.

The trigger was merging the apply-stage PRs by hand before the stage ran. The apply stage parking at all was a separate bug, fixed in `claudinite-lifecycle` 60831.3.

## The fix

The stamp skips a pack that finished the run owing a withheld file, scoped to that pack rather than the whole run. The record stays applicable, so the next cycle stages the delivery again — a merged-but-undelivered PR becomes self-healing instead of a silent permanent loss.

The sweep is deliberately left alone. Its premise — that a staged file from an earlier cycle is a leftover — is correct once the stamp no longer advances, because the same run re-stages the file and `stagedNow` already protects it. Changing the sweep as well would have broken the retired-lane cleanup it exists for.

## Re-reaching the five

Nothing lowers a stamp already written, so the five need a record at a version above where they landed. `2026-09-01-executor-vars-redelivery` reuses the original's `rewrite` rather than restating it, so the two cannot drift, and its `appliesTo` reads the destination's own content — inert on the eight that received the line normally, and safe on a member below 60831.6 where both records are in range.

Named `-redelivery` rather than `-bag-redeliver` because `migrationActive` matches a slug by substring: any name containing the original's slug would keep it reading as active forever, which the record-window test caught.

## Verification

- The stamp test fails on `main` for the right reason (`60831.9` where `60831.5` is owed) and passes here; it also asserts the second cycle re-stages rather than losing the file, and that a pack with nothing withheld is still stamped normally.
- The re-issue test pins that it sits above the original's version, carries an identical rewrite, delivers into a stranded executor, and is inert on a second pass.
- Full suite: 2909 tests, 0 failures.
- `check_the_world`: 0 blocking, 87 advisory — identical to `main` with the branch stashed, so none are this change's.

Confirmed state before the fix, identical on all five (ClaudiniteCanary, hitbut, TLDR, LaughCounter, VascularColoring): no `CLAUDINITE_VARS`, stamped `claudinite-tasks` 60831.9, record absent from the mount, `.claudinite/pending-workflows/` empty. ClaudiniteCanary#311 shows both the staged file and the record as `removed`.

Weekly prose-to-checks sweep over `.claudinite/local/packs` and `packs` (per the [prose-to-checks](packs/claudinite-growth/skills/prose-to-checks/SKILL.md) skill). Surveyed all 34 canon packs plus this repo's two local packs for always-testable working rules that were never converted; converted the two strongest candidates and deleted the prose they now fully cover.

- **`doc-pointer-resolves`** (`.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite`, world scope) — every rule module's `doc:` field must resolve to a real file, repo-root-relative or relative to the rule's own pack (the corpus spells it both ways, inconsistently, so the check accepts whichever interpretation resolves). Replaces the RULES.md line asking a session to "grep for and re-verify every `doc:` field by hand" after a move. Verified silent against all 49 real `doc:` fields currently in the corpus.
- **`shared-tree-immutable`** (`packs/claudinite-lifecycle`, work scope) — flags any branch commit touching `.claudinite/shared/` directly, except the update flow's own commit. Replaces the RULES.md line "Never edit anything there." Ships `blocking`, so per `consumer-safe-change` it needed either a migration record or a rehearsal-fixture discharge; since a work-scope rule is never exercised by the fixture rehearsal (which runs only `selftest` and `check_the_world`, never `check_the_work`), I discharged it with a comment in `vendoring/rehearsal/fixtures.mjs` explaining why rather than fabricating a fixture that would prove nothing — documented in the second commit.

Both checks ship with a see-it-fail fixture (a violating case and a clean case) and were verified silent against the real tree. Full suite (2674 tests), `check_the_work`, and `check_the_world` are all green.

Candidates considered but not converted this run (judgment calls or false-positive risk that didn't clear the bar — logged here rather than a separate backlog issue, since none reached the point of being built and rejected): aws-sam CORS `AllowOrigins`, chrome-extension service-worker module type and `web_accessible_resources` graph, headless-browser hardcoded browser path, macos `command -v swift` and entitlement/runtime-flag pairing, node `--test` path resolution, jwt committed key material, flutter port/plugin boundary, firebase `.gitignore`/ruleset catch-all, static-website root-relative URLs, web-speech `isFinal` trap. Several of these are strong future candidates for the next sweep.

## Changed folders

- **`.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/`** — new `worldRules/doc-pointer-resolves.mjs` check + fixture test; RULES.md loses the paragraph it now covers; VERSIONS.md row.
- **`packs/claudinite-lifecycle/`** — new `workRules/shared-tree-immutable.mjs` check + fixture test; RULES.md loses the paragraph it now covers; README.md rule/check index updated to match; `pack.mjs` version bump + VERSIONS.md row (required — this pack ships to every member).
- **`vendoring/rehearsal/fixtures.mjs`** — a documentation-only comment explaining why work-scope rules need no new fixture shape, discharging `consumer-safe-change` for the new blocking rule.

## Test plan

- [x] `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — 2674 pass, 0 fail
- [x] `node engine/checks/check_the_work.mjs` — clean
- [x] `node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` — 0 blocking
- [x] Both new checks verified silent against the real tree (not just synthetic fixtures)

Closes #1274

Weekly prose-to-checks sweep over `.claudinite/local/packs` and `packs` (per the [prose-to-checks](packs/claudinite-growth/skills/prose-to-checks/SKILL.md) skill). Surveyed all 34 canon packs plus this repo's two local packs for always-testable working rules that were never converted; converted the two strongest candidates and deleted the prose they now fully cover.

- **`doc-pointer-resolves`** (`.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite`, world scope) — every rule module's `doc:` field must resolve to a real file, repo-root-relative or relative to the rule's own pack (the corpus spells it both ways, inconsistently, so the check accepts whichever interpretation resolves). Replaces the RULES.md line asking a session to "grep for and re-verify every `doc:` field by hand" after a move. Verified silent against all 49 real `doc:` fields currently in the corpus.
- **`shared-tree-immutable`** (`packs/claudinite-lifecycle`, work scope) — flags any branch commit touching `.claudinite/shared/` directly, except the update flow's own commit. Replaces the RULES.md line "Never edit anything there." Ships `blocking`, so per `consumer-safe-change` it needed either a migration record or a rehearsal-fixture discharge; since a work-scope rule is never exercised by the fixture rehearsal (which runs only `selftest` and `check_the_world`, never `check_the_work`), I discharged it with a comment in `vendoring/rehearsal/fixtures.mjs` explaining why rather than fabricating a fixture that would prove nothing — documented in the second commit.

Both checks ship with a see-it-fail fixture (a violating case and a clean case) and were verified silent against the real tree. Full suite (2674 tests), `check_the_work`, and `check_the_world` are all green.

Candidates considered but not converted this run (judgment calls or false-positive risk that didn't clear the bar — logged here rather than a separate backlog issue, since none reached the point of being built and rejected): aws-sam CORS `AllowOrigins`, chrome-extension service-worker module type and `web_accessible_resources` graph, headless-browser hardcoded browser path, macos `command -v swift` and entitlement/runtime-flag pairing, node `--test` path resolution, jwt committed key material, flutter port/plugin boundary, firebase `.gitignore`/ruleset catch-all, static-website root-relative URLs, web-speech `isFinal` trap. Several of these are strong future candidates for the next sweep.

## Changed folders

- **`.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/`** — new `worldRules/doc-pointer-resolves.mjs` check + fixture test; RULES.md loses the paragraph it now covers; VERSIONS.md row.
- **`packs/claudinite-lifecycle/`** — new `workRules/shared-tree-immutable.mjs` check + fixture test; RULES.md loses the paragraph it now covers; README.md rule/check index updated to match; `pack.mjs` version bump + VERSIONS.md row (required — this pack ships to every member).
- **`vendoring/rehearsal/fixtures.mjs`** — a documentation-only comment explaining why work-scope rules need no new fixture shape, discharging `consumer-safe-change` for the new blocking rule.

## Test plan

- [x] `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — 2674 pass, 0 fail
- [x] `node engine/checks/check_the_work.mjs` — clean
- [x] `node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` — 0 blocking
- [x] Both new checks verified silent against the real tree (not just synthetic fixtures)

Closes #1274

Only `session-tooling` carried revalidatable claims — `repo-mechanics` and `site-copy` are judgment/process prose with no falsifiable environment facts.

Closes #208

## Verdicts

| Claim (session-tooling) | Probe | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| GITHUB_TOKEN is structurally forbidden from pushing to `.github/workflows/` | `WebSearch` on GitHub's own docs/discussions (WebFetch to `docs.github.com` is itself `EGRESS_BLOCKED` in this sandbox) — confirmed: the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` can never create/update workflow files; only a PAT with `workflow` scope can | `doc-verified` |
| `fields` subset narrows response size on `search_issues` / `list_issues` | Read the live tool schemas via `ToolSearch` — both carry a `fields` array param | `holds` |
| `fields` subset narrows response size on `search_repositories` too | Read the live `search_repositories` schema — **no `fields` param exists**; the actual knob is `minimal_output` (default `true`) | `stale (corrected)` |
| `actions_list` has no `fields`/`minimal_output`, and `per_page` doesn't shrink oversized results | Read the live schema (confirmed no such params) + called `actions_list list_workflow_runs` with `per_page: 3`, got back far more than 3 runs | `holds` |
| For a PR, prefer `get_files`/`get_commits`/`get_check_runs` over `get` | Read the live `pull_request_read` schema — all three methods present | `holds` |
| `WebFetch` egress-blocks some domains with a distinct `EGRESS_BLOCKED` error (not a publisher 403), `gartner.com` among them | Called `WebFetch` on `https://www.gartner.com/` — got back the exact `{"error_type":"EGRESS_BLOCKED",...}` shape named in the rule | `holds` |
| `codeload.github.com` is blocked, `curl … \| tar` returns 403 | `curl`'d a real tarball from `codeload.github.com` for this repo — **200 OK, valid gzip, extracts cleanly** | `stale (corrected — deleted)` |
| `enable_pr_auto_merge` can never arm here because `main` carries no branch-protection rule | No read-only tool in this session's toolset reads branch-protection state, and calling `enable_pr_auto_merge` itself risks actually arming auto-merge on a real PR if the claim is now false (a write side-effect, out of bounds for a probe) | `unprobed (no safe read-only path to repo-specific branch-protection state)` |
| `ScheduleWakeup` requires `prompt` unless `stop: true` | Read the tool's own loaded schema — `prompt` marked "Required unless `stop` is true" | `holds` |
| `search_issues` is natural-language semantic matching, not qualifier filtering | Read the live tool description — verbatim: "Search issues using natural-language semantic matching" | `holds` |
| `list_issues` with `fields`+`perPage:100`, no `state` filter, returns "all 80 issues" in one call | Called it live — `totalCount: 131`, `pageInfo.hasNextPage: true` at `perPage: 100` | `stale (corrected)` |

## Corrections made

1. **`search_repositories` doesn't take `fields`.** Split the "pass a `fields` subset" bullet so it no longer lumps `search_repositories` in with `search_issues`/`list_issues`; named `minimal_output` as its actual (and already-default) size knob.
2. **`codeload.github.com` is no longer blocked.** Deleted the bullet outright — the surface it warned about is gone, so there's nothing left to instruct.
3. **"All 80 issues come back in one call" is now false** (131 issues, already past one page). Replaced the fixed count with a check on `pageInfo.hasNextPage`/`endCursor` so the guidance doesn't just go stale again at the next growth milestone.

Each correction gets a dated row in `session-tooling/VERSIONS.md` (new file — the pack had none yet).

`repo-mechanics` and `site-copy` are untouched — nothing in either pack asserts a fact a platform change could falsify.

## Unrelated fix in the same branch

The session's Stop hook blocked on a pre-existing `reference-integrity` finding unrelated to the above: `product-wiki/brand/README.md` still linked to `.claudinite-checks.json`, which was folded into `.claudinite-settings.json` back in `0b2fc78` and never updated at the call site. Fixed the one link (second commit).

`node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` exits clean on this branch.

## Note on #208

This session could not run the queue's `converge-item.mjs` step — it needs direct `GITHUB_TOKEN` REST API access, which this execution channel doesn't have (MCP-only). Left a comment on #208 explaining the blocker instead of hand-converging it; it needs a person (or a run from a context with real token access) to close it out.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

- session-start-hook: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code on the web. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for Claude Code on the web, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during web sessions.

- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.

content.text:
You're right, and the correction matters. "Quiet and uniform" described the *shape of my table*, not the fleet. Five of thirteen members are missing a capability the other eight have, and the queue has recorded that delivery as `done` — that is a **broken, divergent fleet**, and 13/13 on version stamps is exactly the misleading number that hid it in the first place. I'll report fleet health by what members actually carry, not by what they claim.

On your question: I have real doubts, so I'm doing both — an independent review, and my own end-to-end simulation.

input.prompt:
You are adversarially reviewing a proposed fix in the repo at /home/user/Claudinite. Be skeptical; the author (another Claude session) may be wrong. Do NOT edit any files — read and reason only. Report findings, not reassurance.

CONTEXT — the production incident:
Claudinite is a "canon" repo distributing versioned packs to 13 member repos via a vendored mount at `.claudinite/shared/`. A migration record `packs/claudinite-tasks/migrations/2026-08-31-executor-vars-bag/` rewrites each member's live `.github/workflows/claudinite-executor.yml` to add a `CLAUDINITE_VARS: ${{ toJSON(vars) }}` line.

Because a converge's GITHUB_TOKEN may not push under `.github/workflows/`, the "withhold lane" stages such a write to `.claudinite/pending-workflows/` and raises an `apply-stage` terminal; a later agent session with a stronger credential moves it into place.

On 5 of 13 members the apply-stage session parked instead of delivering (a separate bug, since fixed). A human then merged those update PRs by hand. Result:
- the merge advanced the member's stamp for pack `claudinite-tasks` to 60831.6+ (now 60831.9)
- `migrationApplies` is `want > have` (engine/checks/helpers/active-migrations.mjs), so the record fell out of range, stopped applying and stopped being vendored
- the next converge's staging sweep deleted the staged file as a "leftover"
- net: 5 members permanently lack the line, with no copy of the content left and no record that can reach them. Everything stayed green.

THE PROPOSED FIX is on branch `claude/github-secrets-env-vars-xms47c` (2 commits ahead of origin/main). Read it with:
  git log --oneline origin/main..claude/github-secrets-env-vars-xms47c
  git diff origin/main...claude/github-secrets-env-vars-xms47c

It has two parts:
1. In `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/pack-update.mjs`: track which pack each withheld path came from (via `flowOf(m.dir).pack` around the `applyMigration` loop) and SKIP stamping that pack's version at the stamp step.
2. A new record `packs/claudinite-tasks/migrations/2026-09-01-executor-vars-redelivery/` at version 60901.1 (above where the 5 members landed at 60831.9), which spreads the original record's `rewrite` and relies on `appliesTo` testing the destination's own content so it no-ops on the 8 healthy members.

ANSWER THESE, each with file:line evidence and an explicit verdict:

A) Does part 2 actually re-reach the 5 stranded members? Trace concretely: does the new record get VENDORED into a member stamped claudinite-tasks=60831.9 (check the vendor-set / `migrationApplies` path), does it get selected by `packRecordsInGap`, does its rewrite get withheld+staged, and does an apply-stage terminal get raised? Name where each step happens.

B) THE ONE I MOST DOUBT — after part 1 holds back the stamp, what ever re-stamps the pack? Trace the cycle AFTER the apply stage successfully delivers the file: does the member's claudinite-tasks version ever reach 60901.1, or does it stay pinned at 60831.9 forever, re-staging and re-raising an apply stage every single night? Is there an unbounded loop or daily PR churn? Does `appliesTo` returning false prevent the withhold on the next cycle (and therefore allow the stamp)?

C) What ELSE reads these version stamps and could now misbehave because a converged member deliberately reports an older version? Specifically check `packs/claudinite-fleet-sheepdog/tasks/fleet-baseline/follow-to-current.mjs` (does a withheld member now read as "did-not-converge" and fail a fleet baseline?), plus any staleness/drift checks, the dashboard, and `minEngineVersion` handling. Search broadly for readers of installed pack versions.

D) Does the fix actually close the reported bug, or only narrow it? Find any remaining path where a withheld file is still lost: e.g. a withheld write that comes from something OTHER than a migration record (so `flowOf(m.dir).pack` never attributes it); a record whose `dir` doesn't start with `packs/` (what does `flowOf` return then, and what happens?); an ENGINE-flow record withholding; or the staging sweep deleting a file in a cycle where the record legitimately did not re-stage.

E) Is the author's stated reason for NOT also fixing the sweep sound? They argue the sweep is safe once the stamp is held, because the same run re-stages and `stagedNow` protects it. Attack that argument.

Useful commands: `node --test engine-tests/pack-update.test.mjs`, and read `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/pack-update.mjs`, `engine/checks/helpers/active-migrations.mjs`, `engine/migrations/registry.mjs`, `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/tasks/update/task.md`, `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/terminals.mjs`.

Finish with a blunt verdict on each of A–E: does this fix work, and does it fully close the bug? Flag anything that would make you refuse to merge it.

 — a pack imports only its own files and the engine surface (pack-independence)"
```

The re-issued record imports the original. But the vendor set only carries records that still **apply** — and the original (60831.6) does not apply to a member at 60831.9, so it is never vendored there. The import dangles, the mount fails pack-independence, and `packUpdate` returns `needs-human`: **the converge refuses to land at all.**

As written, #1546 would not have fixed five members. It would have wedged all thirteen — and the canon's own rule names that outcome exactly: *"A pack that fails to load … the converge refuses to land at all, and the member cannot receive the pack version that would have fixed it."* Every test passed because in the canon tree both files exist.

Fixing it the way the corpus prescribes — duplicate, with a drift guard.

# Update — the apply stage

The deterministic half already ran. Preprocessing converged this repo's mount to the
canon's current engine and pack versions, ran the version-ranged migrations, gated the
result on the converged tree's own `selftest --strict`, and opened the update PR. The
work item names the branch and says which packs moved.

**You are here for one of two reasons**, and the issue says which:

- **Withheld workflow files** — content the deterministic half already decided but its
  Action token is refused for. Nothing here needs judgment; you are the credential.
- **A pack's updated rules have met content this repo authored** and the canon has never
  seen. This is the half that needs judgment, and it is all of the judgment there is.

## 1. Read why you are here

The item's **Why the agent is here** section names the terminal and the packs
whose versions moved. That is binding scope — do not widen it.

## 2. Deliver the withheld workflow files

Only if the item's reason names them. A file under `.claudinite/pending-workflows/` is
content the deterministic half already computed and decided; it sits there because the
Action token that pushed the branch may not write under `.github/workflows/` and GitHub
rejects the WHOLE ref for trying, so putting it in the pushed tree would have failed the
entire update. You hold a credential that may write there. That is the only reason this
step is yours.

For each staged file: move `.claudinite/pending-workflows/<name>` to
`.github/workflows/<name>`, and leave the staging directory empty.

**Do not edit the content, and do not judge it.** It is what the canon computed for this
member, secrets and all; a session rewriting it is a second author of a file that has
exactly one. If the move is not obviously right — the branch carries a staged file the
item's reason does not name, or the destination already differs in a way you cannot
explain — that is the case for §5, not for improvising.

## 3. Apply the new rules

Only if the issue's reason names a migration record — it names them by path, e.g.
`packs/basics/migrations/2026-08-13-something`. **Read that record** at
`.claudinite/shared/<path>/migration.mjs`: its `applyStage.instructions` say what its
author wanted done, in their words, and are the specific half of this section. The
record is on the branch you were given because the update that raised it vendored it
there. A record the issue names but the branch does not carry is a park
(§5) — guessing at what its author wanted is worse than reporting it missing.

Then, on that branch:

- Bring this repo's own content in line with the updated pack rules, and repair the
  tests those rules break.
- Nothing outside that scope. No new features, no unrelated tidy-ups, no rewriting a
  member-authored local pack beyond what the new rules require.

## 4. Verify the executor routine

The one check no Action can make. This repo's executor routine is fired by an API
call to the endpoint its config names, and it is not a GitHub artifact — only a
session can see it. Confirm it exists and that its whole stored prompt is the one
line pointing at the mounted queue instructions
(`.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/instructions.md`): everything a task
session does comes from that file, so a prompt carrying instructions of its own is
behavior nobody reviews. Report what you found either way.

## 5. End green, or park

Run this repo's checks. Green: push to the branch, then hand the PR to the shared
delivery procedure — `deliver-pr.md`, at the root of the claudinite-tasks pack
(`.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/deliver-pr.md`; the canon runs it from
`packs/claudinite-tasks/`) — and do what it says. Nothing else will land this PR:
the deterministic half arms auto-merge only on a `merge` terminal, and yours was
`apply-stage`, so it sits unarmed until you deliver it.

Not green, or a repair you are not sure of: leave the PR open, label
it `task:status:needs-human-decision`, and say in one comment what is unresolved. A withheld workflow you did
not deliver is "not green" — it stays owed, and the next cycle will stage it again.

**Why the delivery is yours to run rather than left for later.** An unmerged PR is not lost — the next
cycle's disposal merges a green one. But `update` is a **daily** task, so "the next
cycle" is up to a day away, and until then a workflow you moved into
`.github/workflows/` on the branch is not in `.github/workflows/` on `main`. That
standing ~24h offset between a run's output and the member's `main` is the exact defect
`landDelivery` was written to close for the deterministic half (#649,
`packs/claudinite-tasks/land-pr.mjs`): *the evidence that settles it does not take a day to
arrive*. The same reasoning binds here — the only difference is that you hold the
credential, so you are the one who acts on it.

Every non-green end looks the same here, and that is the point — a repair nobody
verified is not a smaller problem than a red check, it is the same problem with less
evidence.

Pushed. Answering your two questions with what the simulations actually showed. ## Was #1546 going to fix this? **No — as you suspected, it was broken.** Running a real converge against a member tree in the five's exact state returned: ``` status: needs-human "…executor-vars-redelivery/migration.mjs imports ../2026-08-31-executor-vars-bag/migration.mjs … which the vendor set does not carry — a pack imports only its own files" ``` The re-issued record imported the original to avoid restating it. The vendor set carries only records that still **apply** to a member — and the members this record exists for are precisely the ones the original no longer applies to. The import dangles, the pack fails `pack-independence`, and the converge refuses to land. It would have **wedged all thirteen members instead of repairing five.** The full 2914-test suite was green, because in the canon tree both files exist. Only a converge driven against a member tree stamped past the original exposes it. That's the canon's own rule — *survey by reading each file; a miss is not evidence* — and a green suite was not evidence either. Now fixed: the block is copied, pinned by a rewrite-equality test, plus a new test refusing **any** record that imports another record, seen failing on this exact import. ## Does it fix #1545? **Yes — and I can now show it rather than argue it.** Three simulated lifecycles against real code: 
STRANDED member (the five)         cycle 1    cycle 2 (after delivery)   cycle 3
  withheld                         yes        no                         no
  apply stage raised               yes        no                         no
  claudinite-tasks stamp           60831.9    60901.1                    60901.1
  live executor has VARS           no         YES                        YES

STRANDED, apply stage still fails  cycle 1    cycle 2                    cycle 3
  withheld / staged                yes        yes (re-staged)            yes
  stamp                            60831.9    60831.9                    60831.9
  file lost                        no         no                         no

HEALTHY member (the eight)         cycle 1    cycle 2
  withheld                         no         no
  stamp                            60901.1    60901.1
The middle case is #1545 itself: previously that path deleted the staged file and put the record permanently out of range. Now the delivery stays owed indefinitely and re-stages every cycle. The top case answers my own biggest doubt — the held stamp **does** catch up once delivery succeeds, so there's no pinned-forever member and no nightly PR churn. ## On the fleet-health framing Taking your correction as standing: I'll describe fleet health by what members **carry**, never by what they stamp — and a split is broken until every member has the capability, not "converged with a variance." The version stamps reading 13/13 while five lacked the line is the precise shape of the misreport, and it's now the bug's own headline. One caveat I won't paper over: an independent adversarial review of this branch is still running, specifically probing whether holding the stamp breaks anything else that reads versions — `fleet-baseline`'s follow-to-current is the one I'd bet on, since a withholding member would now read as "did-not-converge" for a cycle. I'll report what it finds rather than pre-empt it. > ⚠️ Do not merge yet: > • [#1546](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1546) updated (`ced6e37`) — the version you were about to approve would have wedged the fleet. > • 2915 tests pass, 0 blocking, advisories unchanged from `main`; the new import guard was seen failing before passing. > • **Fleet is broken and divergent**: 5 of 13 members lack `CLAUDINITE_VARS`, and their work items are closed `task:status:done` for a delivery that never happened. > • Adversarial review still running — may surface further problems with holding the stamp, `fleet-baseline` most likely. > • PR body still describes the import-based record; I'll correct it once the review lands.

content.text:
## Verdict summary

Full suite is green on the branch (`2915/2915`, ~104s). The mechanism is sound in the happy path, but **part 1 introduces a new silent-stall path in the worker that the author never tested**, and **part 1 breaks the fleet-baseline follow for exactly the members it exists to help**. I would not merge as-is.

---

### A) Does part 2 re-reach the 5 stranded members? — **YES, traced end to end.**

1. **Vendored.** `vendoring/compute-vendor-set.mjs:96` — `if (isRecordOfFlow(relDir, entry.name) && !migrationApplies(rel, {installed, today})) continue;`. For the new record `want=60901.1`, member `have=60831.9` → `versionAbove` true (`engine/checks/helpers/active-migrations.mjs:189`) → the directory is walked and ships.
2. **Selected.** `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/pack-update.mjs:61-67` (`packRecordsInGap`) filters `flow==='pack' && pack==='claudinite-tasks' && migrationApplies` → the record is in `plan[].records` (`:94`), so `wanted`/`specs` at `:230-231` load it. Note this runs from a **fresh canon clone** (worker.mjs:160-166), and `updates/` is excluded from the vendor set (`compute-vendor-set.mjs:44 UPDATES_DIR`), so selection is never limited by the member's mount.
3. **Applied + withheld.** `appliesTo` in the spread original (`2026-08-31-executor-vars-bag/migration.mjs:43-47`) reads `.github/workflows/claudinite-executor.yml` and returns true iff `HOLD` present and no `CLAUDINITE_VARS:` — true for the 5. `applyRewrites` (registry.mjs:~130-165) writes; `write` at pack-update.mjs:247-251 routes the `.github/workflows/` prefix to `stagedAt(p)` and pushes to `withheld`.
4. **Terminal raised.** `applyStageFor(specs, withheld)` (`:143-165`) → `needed:true` from `withheld.length` alone; `terminalFor` (`terminals.mjs:34-41`) yields `apply-stage`.

Two nits, neither fatal:
- The re-issue carries no `applyStage` (it spreads the original, which has none), so `applyStageFor`'s `packs` is `[]` (`:159`) — the work item's "binding scope" (`task.md:22-24`) names no pack. Pre-existing, but this is the second record to hit it.
- `assert.deepEqual(reissue.rewrite, original.rewrite)` in `engine-tests/migrations.test.mjs` is vacuous — the spread makes it the *same object reference*. It proves nothing. (Safe only because the replacements are literal `from`/`to`; a global `RegExp` shared across two records would share `lastIndex`.)

### B) What re-stamps the pack? — **It terminates, but there is a real silent-stall path.**

Happy path terminates correctly: cycle N stages, stamp held (`:313`), apply stage delivers to `.github/workflows/` and merges. Cycle N+1: `appliesTo` now false → `applyRewrites` returns `[]` → nothing withheld → `owesDelivery` empty → `packVersions['claudinite-tasks'] = '60901.1'` written. **No unbounded loop; `appliesTo` returning false is exactly what releases the stamp.** Correct.

**But here is the hole.** Consider the incident's own shape, which is still reachable: the apply-stage session parks without moving the file, and the *next* cycle's `disposeOpenPull` merges the green PR anyway (`packs/claudinite-tasks/land-pr.mjs:407-425` — `pullDisposition` reads only CI runs and the delivery setting; it does not look at a park label). Main now carries the staged file and the **held** stamp. On the following cycle:

- the record still applies (stamp held — by design),
- `write` re-stages **byte-identical** content over the file already in `main`,
- the stamp is **not** written (held),
- so `worker.mjs:199-202`: `const changed = git status --porcelain` is **empty**, and `if (!changed && terminal.action !== 'apply-stage'-aware) { return; }` — the guard only exempts `needs-human`. The worker returns **before** opening the PR, and the apply-stage request file is written at `:239-243`, *after* PR creation. **No PR, no work item, no apply stage, exit 0.**

Before this change that state was unreachable, because the withholding cycle *always* wrote the stamp, guaranteeing `changed` was non-empty and the apply stage got requested. Part 1 removes the only thing that made the tree dirty on a re-staging cycle. In practice canon usually moves daily so the mount re-vendor dirties the tree — but "usually" is what this whole incident is about. **This is a defect the fix should have closed and did not; the author's test (`engine-tests/pack-update.test.mjs`, the new case) asserts `again.withheld` at the *flow* level and never exercises the worker.**

No daily PR churn otherwise: `disposeOpenPull` keeps one PR alive at a time (worker.mjs:135-149).

### C) Other stamp readers — **one real regression, two cosmetic.**

- **`follow-to-current.mjs` — genuinely broken by part 1.** `readFreshness` (`:75-79`) → `classifyFreshness` (`drift-issues.mjs:76-108`) returns `behind` for any pack where canon > installed. A member that legitimately converged but is holding `claudinite-tasks` at 60831.9 **can never read `FRESH`**, so `followToCurrent` burns the entire budget and reports `DID_NOT_CONVERGE` (`:44`, `isSuccess` at `:47`). That is precisely the forced fleet-baseline sweep that would be used to push this redelivery out — it will report the 5 target members as failures. The branch contains no accommodation for a deliberately-held stamp anywhere in sheepdog.
- **`fleet-roster` drift issues** (`drift-issues.mjs:140-260`): a held member is `behind` → a drift issue is opened/kept on it with the `behind` fix text ("the self-refresh is not landing… check the repo's recent scheduler runs"), which is now actively misleading — the self-refresh *is* landing. It self-closes once the stamp catches up (≥1 extra day, or forever in the B stall).
- **Dashboard** `packs/claudinite-dashboard/fleet.mjs:87-113` → `state: 'behind'` for the same window. Cosmetic.
- **`minEngineVersion`**: `planPackUpdates` (`pack-update.mjs:78-96`) reads `installed.engineVersion`, not pack versions — unaffected. The engine stamp is written unconditionally in `engine-update.mjs:206-208` and is untouched by this fix.
- The `stamp` signal exposes `packVersions` (`packs/claudinite-tasks/signals/index.mjs:325-327`) but the only consumer is `update/task.mjs:50`, which reads `stamp.present`. Safe.

### D) Closed, or narrowed? — **Narrowed. Four residual loss/mis-attribution paths.**

1. **Non-pack (engine) records get no hold.** `flowOf` returns `{flow:'engine'}` with no `pack` (`active-migrations.mjs:135-139`), and the new guard is `if (pack && withheld.length > before)` — silently no-op. The engine flow itself can't withhold (`engine-update.mjs:192` passes `env: {}`, so `applyRewrites`/`applyMaterializations` emit `SKIPPED …` and drop the write) while `engine-update.mjs:206-208` stamps unconditionally. Same bug class, one flow over, untouched.
2. **Cross-pack withhold attribution is wrong.** `write` only pushes to `withheld` when `!withheld.includes(p)` (`:250`). Two records from *different packs* naming the same workflow path: the second's `put(stagedAt(p), c)` **overwrites** the staged content, `withheld.length` does not grow, so the second pack is **not** added to `owesDelivery` and **is** stamped — while its content is the one staged and the first pack's content is silently gone. The counter should be keyed per-path-per-pack, not on array length.
3. **`appliesTo` going false for a reason other than delivery still loses the staged copy.** Any drift in the anchor (`HOLD` line renamed, the wiring converge regenerating the region, someone adding a `CLAUDINITE_VARS:` comment) makes `appliesTo` false → no re-stage → sweep deletes the staged file (`:284-288`) → `owesDelivery` empty → stamp advances → record permanently out of range. Byte-for-byte the reported bug, with a different trigger.
4. **`applyRewrites` `if (text == null) continue`** (registry.mjs) — a member whose executor is momentarily unreadable/renamed produces the same outcome as (3).

### E) The author's reason for not fixing the sweep — **unsound.**

The claim is: *the sweep is safe once the stamp is held, because the same run re-stages and `stagedNow` protects it.* That argument is circular. `stagedNow` (`:284`) is built from `withheld`, which is populated **only if the record re-stages**. input.title: The staging sweep deletes on "I didn't write it this pass", which is not the same as "it was delivered"
input.body:
Follow-up to #1545, which fixed the version-stamp half of that incident. The sweep's own criterion is still wrong, and it can reproduce the same silent loss from a different trigger.

## The criterion

`packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/pack-update.mjs` sweeps the staging directory of anything this run did not stage:

```js
const stagedNow = new Set(withheld.map(stagedAt));
for (const stale of stagedFiles(targetRoot)) {
  if (stagedNow.has(stale)) continue;
  rmSync(join(targetRoot, stale), { force: true });
}
```

Its comment states the premise: *"a file staged by an earlier cycle was either delivered or abandoned, and either way the record that staged it would stage it again."*

That conflates two opposite facts. "This run did not stage it" is true both when the file **was delivered** (good — sweep it) and when the record **stopped matching for some other reason** (bad — this is the only copy of computed content).

## Where it still loses content

`appliesTo` on the vars-bag records tests `text.includes(HOLD) && !text.includes('CLAUDINITE_VARS:')`. It goes false for reasons other than a successful delivery:

- the anchor line drifts — the operator hold is renamed, or the wiring converge regenerates the region
- someone adds a `CLAUDINITE_VARS:` comment, or a partial edit
- the executor is momentarily unreadable or renamed, so `applyRewrites` hits `if (text == null) continue`

In each case the record does not re-stage, the sweep deletes the staged file, and — because nothing was withheld — the pack is stamped, putting the record out of range. That is byte-for-byte the #1545 outcome with a different trigger.

#1545's stamp hold narrows the window but does not make the criterion correct; the protection (`stagedNow`) is conditional on precisely the premise that failed.

## The fix

Delete a staged file only when the destination demonstrably carries its content, rather than when this pass happened not to write it. A file whose destination still lacks it is an outstanding delivery, not a leftover.

This needs care with one existing behaviour: `engine-tests/pack-update.test.mjs`'s *"the retired staging directory is swept, whatever an earlier cycle left in it"* covers a genuine leftover from the retired lane whose destination will never match. That case wants an explicit rule (out of range for the right reason), not the current catch-all.

Also worth scoping: the sweep is unconditional across flows, with nothing limiting it to files the pack flow owns.

## Second, smaller gap

An **engine**-flow record gets no hold at all. `flowOf` returns `{ flow: 'engine' }` with no `pack`, and the guard added in #1545 is `if (owedBy)`. Today the engine flow cannot withhold — `engine-update.mjs` passes `env: {}`, so workflow writes are skipped — while it stamps unconditionally. If the engine flow ever gains the withhold lane, it inherits the original bug.

input.title: A member owing a withheld delivery reads as "behind", so a fleet baseline reports it as failed
input.body:
Follow-up to #1545. That fix stops a pack being stamped while it still owes a withheld workflow file, so the record stays in range and the delivery is re-staged rather than lost. The consequence is a member that has converged correctly but deliberately reports an older pack version for a cycle — and sheepdog has no way to tell that apart from a member that is failing to converge.

## What misreads it

`packs/claudinite-fleet-sheepdog/tasks/fleet-roster/drift-issues.mjs`, `classifyFreshness`, compares each installed pack version against canon and returns `behind` on any gap. A member holding `claudinite-tasks` while canon has moved can never read `FRESH`.

Two things follow:

1. **`fleet-baseline` reports the member as failed.** `follow-to-current.mjs` polls freshness until every dispatched member reaches canon's versions, then reports `did-not-converge` for those that did not. A member that withheld a file will not reach them until the *next* cycle, after the apply stage delivers — so a forced baseline reports it as a failure. That is precisely the lever used to push a withheld delivery out, reporting the target members as broken.

2. **The roster opens a drift issue with misleading remediation.** The `behind` fix text tells the reader the self-refresh is not landing and to check the repo's recent scheduler runs. The self-refresh *is* landing; a delivery is pending on another credential. It self-closes once the stamp catches up, having sent someone to look at the wrong thing.

## Why "behind" is not simply wrong

The member genuinely has not received the version — that is the honest reading, and #1545 exists because the opposite reading (stamped, therefore delivered) is what made a broken fleet look healthy. This is not a request to report such a member as fresh.

What is missing is a **third state**. "Converged, delivery pending" is neither `fresh` nor `behind`, and collapsing it into `behind` loses the distinction that decides whether anyone should act.

## Shape of the fix

Make the hold visible so it can be classified rather than inferred: have the member record that a delivery is owed (and for which pack), and give `classifyFreshness` an `owes-delivery` state with its own remediation text. `follow-to-current` then treats it as a terminal, non-failing outcome — the baseline's job is done once the deterministic half has landed and the apply stage is raised.

Worth deciding at the same time: whether a member that has owed a delivery for several cycles should escalate, since that is a real stall and currently indistinguishable from one healthy pending cycle.

input.body:
Closes #1545

Five members are stamped past `claudinite-tasks` 60831.6 with no `CLAUDINITE_VARS` line in their live executor, and no converge can reach them. This fixes the cause and re-opens a route to the five.

## The defect

A migration record targeting `.github/workflows/` cannot be written by the converge — GitHub rejects the whole ref for a `GITHUB_TOKEN` push under that path — so the withhold lane stages it to `.claudinite/pending-workflows/` and the apply stage delivers it on a credential that may write there.

The run stamped the owning pack regardless. That claims a delivery that has not happened, and it is unrecoverable rather than merely early:

1. `migrationApplies` is `want > have`, so the stamp immediately puts the record out of range — it stops applying and stops vendoring.
2. The next cycle's staging sweep reads the undelivered file as a leftover and deletes it.

Both copies of the content are then gone. Every signal stays green: the run succeeds, the stamp reads current, and `fleet-baseline` — which follows members to canon's stamped versions — reports success. A forced baseline did exactly that in 4m35s while five members were missing the delivery.

## The fix

**The stamp** skips a pack that finished the run owing a withheld file, scoped to that pack. The record stays applicable, so the next cycle stages the delivery again — a merged-but-undelivered PR becomes self-healing instead of a silent permanent loss. Attribution happens as each write occurs rather than by counting `withheld` afterwards, because that list is de-duplicated by path: two records from different packs naming one workflow path would otherwise stamp the pack whose content is the one actually staged.

**The worker's "nothing changed" guard** now lets an apply-stage terminal through. Holding the stamp removed the only thing that reliably dirtied the tree on a withholding cycle, so a re-staging cycle can leave `git status` clean — and the guard returns before the PR is opened, while the apply-stage request is written after it. Left unfixed, this fix would have reintroduced the same silent loss one step further along.

## Re-reaching the five

Nothing lowers a stamp already written, so the five need a record above where they landed. `2026-09-01-executor-vars-redelivery` carries the rewrite at 60901.1, and its `appliesTo` reads the destination's own content — inert on the eight that received the line normally, and safe on a member below 60831.6 where both records are in range.

The block is **copied rather than imported**. An import of the original resolves in the canon but not on a member: the vendor set carries only records that still apply, and the members this exists for are exactly the ones the original no longer applies to. The import dangles, the pack fails `pack-independence`, and `packUpdate` returns `needs-human` — the converge stops landing entirely, wedging all thirteen members instead of repairing five. The copy is pinned by a rewrite-equality assertion plus a new test refusing any record that imports another record.

Named `-redelivery` rather than `-bag-redeliver` because `migrationActive` matches a slug by substring: any name containing the original's slug would keep it reading as active forever.

## Verification

Lifecycle simulations driving the real flow against a member tree in the five's exact state (`claudinite-tasks` 60831.9, executor without the line):

| | cycle 1 | cycle 2 | cycle 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Stranded, apply stage delivers** | withheld, stamp held 60831.9 | stamp 60901.1, line present | stable |
| **Stranded, apply stage fails again** | withheld, stamp held | re-staged, nothing lost | re-staged |
| **Healthy (the eight)** | inert, stamp 60901.1 | stable | — |

The middle row is the reported bug: that path previously deleted the staged file and put the record permanently out of range.

- Every new test seen failing first, on the real defect — the stamp (`60831.9` where `60831.5` is owed), the sibling import, the worker guard reverted to its old condition, and the attribution reverted to the count.
- Full suite: 2917 tests, 0 failures. `check_the_world`: 0 blocking, 87 advisory — identical to `main` with the branch stashed.

## Deliberately not in this PR

Both found by an adversarial review of this branch and filed rather than folded in:

- **#1555** — the staging sweep deletes on "I didn't write it this pass", which is not "it was delivered". The stamp hold narrows that window without making the criterion correct, and `appliesTo` going false for a reason *other* than delivery still loses the staged copy.
- **#1556** — a member owing a withheld delivery reads as `behind`, so `fleet-baseline` reports it as `did-not-converge` and the roster opens a drift issue with misleading remediation. Needs a third state, not a re-classification as fresh.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

content.text: Let me verify the one thing that decides this — which of my two code changes reaches a member on the *first* run, since they travel by different lanes.

content.text:
Verified, and it matters: my two changes travel by **different lanes**. 
packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/pack-update.mjs   NOT vendored (compute-vendor-set.mjs:106
  → the stamp hold                                    skips UPDATES_DIR); loaded from a fresh
                                                      canon clone → live on merge, every member

packs/claudinite-lifecycle/tasks/update/worker.mjs   vendored; the running process uses the
  → the apply-stage guard exemption                   member's OLD copy → live only from cycle 2
So cycle 1 runs **new stamp logic on an old worker**. That's survivable only because cycle 1's tree is dirty anyway (it vendors the new record and new pack versions), so the un-exempted `!changed` guard can't fire. Cycle 2 has the new worker, because `claudinite-lifecycle` stamps normally — only `claudinite-tasks` is held. The ordering works, but by a narrow margin rather than by design. ## So: will it align all repos to healthy? **Probably — but not certainly, and not in one step.** Three things stand between merge and a healthy fleet. **1. It takes two converges per member, not one.** Cycle 1 stages and holds the stamp; the apply stage delivers; cycle 2 stamps `60901.1`. A member is only fully healthy after the second. A baseline run watches for the first. **2. The final step is the one that already failed once.** Delivery depends on an agent apply-stage session moving the file. On these five that session parked in August. The brief that caused it is fixed and confirmed present on all five (`claudinite-lifecycle` 60831.3), and eight members did deliver successfully — but this exact path has never run green on these five. I can't tell you it will work; I can tell you the known cause is removed. **3. The baseline will report failure even if it succeeds.** This is [#1556](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1556), and it's now directly in your way: `follow-to-current` polls until every member reaches canon's stamped versions. The five will be *deliberately* holding `claudinite-tasks` at 60831.9 during exactly that window, so the run burns its budget and exits `did-not-converge` on the five — a red run that looks identical to the genuine failure it had last time. You would not be able to distinguish success from failure by reading the baseline's own result. That third point changes my recommendation about ordering. The baseline's verdict is unusable for this rollout, so the check that matters is reading the five members' live `.github/workflows/claudinite-executor.yml` for the line — which is the health measure you told me to use, not the stamp. ## What "healthy" then means Aligned is all 13 carrying `CLAUDINITE_VARS` **and** stamped `60901.1`. Merging #1546 plus a forced baseline plus a successful apply stage on each of five gets there. Merging alone does not — it only makes the repair possible. And two things stay unhealthy regardless: [#1555](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1555) means the same silent loss can recur from a different trigger, and the five work items remain closed `task:status:done` for a delivery that never happened — no mechanism will reopen them.

Fastest to a repaired fleet if the apply stage works, but the baseline will report the five as did-not-converge whether it worked or not, so I would verify by reading each member's live executor file instead of trusting the run. # Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.

# Merge to main

If the project's own `CLAUDE.md` names a merge-policy file, that file overrides the divergent
points below (merge method, CI gating). Don't go hunting for one it doesn't name.
